subject.title: [RFC] Agent Teleconference — minimum-viable scoped meeting primitive with working prototype

question: Should OpenClaw accept a first-party core/CLI meeting lifecycle primitive for agent teleconferences, and if so what storage, authorization, transcript, and handoff-layer shape should it use?
rationale: Current code has the lower-level delivery primitives, but adding durable cross-agent meetings changes core CLI/API surface, runtime state, transcript handling, and security boundaries that cannot be chosen safely by automation.

options.title: Approve a narrow core lifecycle layer
options.body: Define meet/dial/pickup/send/wrap/list/show/transcript as a minimal layer over existing session delivery, using canonical storage and explicit auth/transcript policy before code lands.

options.title: Route to plugin/API work first
options.body: Keep core lean and ask for plugin or SDK gaps to be solved before promoting teleconference verbs into first-party OpenClaw.

options.title: Defer under broader multi-agent architecture
options.body: Close or pause this RFC in favor of #35203 if maintainers want meeting lifecycle to wait for a larger collaboration architecture.

recommendation.title: Approve a narrow core lifecycle layer
recommendation.body: Define meet/dial/pickup/send/wrap/list/show/transcript as a minimal layer over existing session delivery, using canonical storage and explicit auth/transcript policy before code lands.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete provided the concrete scoping review on this RFC and the related lower-level handoff proposal.
